figureObjective: Summarize conditional fission-chain feedback, neutron regulation, and residual decay heat without providing reactor design parameters.

claims.text: A self-sustaining chain requires enough released neutrons to induce later fissions; moderation and absorption regulate feedback, but stopping the chain does not remove decay heat.
Tokens and reactor silhouettes are qualitative system roles, not counts, geometry, operating parameters, or a safety case.

anchors.normalizedText: Water slows neutrons, control rods absorb neutrons to regulate flux, and radioactive fission products continue generating heat after the chain terminates.

elements.meaning: Neutron-induced splitting with fragments, energy, and emitted neutrons.
Subset of emitted neutrons that induce subsequent fissions.
Moderator and control rods regulating neutron behavior in the cited reactor context.
Heat from radioactive fission products after chain termination.

allowedVariation.rule: Fission, feedback, regulation, and residual-heat layers may be rearranged if causal order remains clear.
Token colors and branch spacing may vary without encoding probability, flux, power, or critical mass.
Generic tokens, water band, rod silhouettes, containment outline, and warning icon establish roles but carry no facility or measurement evidence.

mutations.description: State that stopping the chain or inserting rods immediately removes all heat.
Use exact token counts or geometry to assert multiplication factor, reaction rate, critical mass, or power.
Use smoke, facility photos, heat maps, gauges, or scaled containment as accident, dose, operating, or safety evidence.
